title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node II

content.problemStatement:
A binary tree is given as a flat integer array named `tree`, using complete-binary-tree (heap) indexing:

- the root sits at index 0
- a node at index `i` has its left child at index `2*i+1` and right child at index `2*i+2`
- a child index only counts as real if it's within the array bounds **and** its value isn't the sentinel `-101`
- `-101` means "no node here" - real node values always fall between -100 and 100, so -101 can never be a genuine value
- unlike a perfect binary tree, any node may be missing either child, both children, or neither - the shape is arbitrary

**Connect every node to the nearest node to its right on the same level (there might be gaps between them, since some nodes on a level can be missing children), and build and return a new array with the exact same shape (same length, same positions) as `tree`, where each position that held a real node now holds the value of the nearest node to its right on the same level, or -1 if no such node exists.**

Positions that were sentinel or missing in the input should stay exactly -101 in the output.
constraints: every real node value is in the range -100 to 100
the sentinel value -101 marks a missing node and never appears as a real value
the tree may be of any shape, not just a perfect binary tree
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: 1 is alone on level 0; 2's nearest right neighbor on level 1 is 3; 4's nearest right neighbor on level 2 is 5 (skipping the missing children of node 3)
9's nearest right neighbor is 20; 15's nearest right neighbor is 7; the two sentinel positions stay -101
the only node is alone on its level

code.Python3:
# Time:  O(n)
# Space: O(1)

# Definition for a Node.
class Node(object):
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right
        self.next = next


class Solution(object):
    # @param root, a tree node
    # @return nothing
    def connect(self, root):
        head = root
        pre = Node(0)
        cur = pre
        while root:
            while root:
                if root.left:
                    cur.next = root.left
                    cur = cur.next
                if root.right:
                    cur.next = root.right
                    cur = cur.next
                root = root.next
            root, cur = pre.next, pre
            cur.next = None
        return head

hints: Identify the search space and verify that the condition is monotonic (true...true...false...false).
Be mindful of integer overflow when computing mid: use mid = left + (right - left) // 2.
Ensure the termination condition (left <= right vs left < right) correctly handles boundary elements.
